observation: The Decider defaults to 'medium confidence — proceed with caution.' This is a hedge, not a decision. Medium confidence should be rare, not default.
adjustment: Force binary: high (proceed) or low (stop). Medium only when genuinely split.

observation: The Dreamer proposes 3 options ranked by simplicity, but the Doubter attacks all 3 equally instead of focusing on the one the Dreamer recommends. Debate spreads thin.
adjustment: Doubter should attack the recommended option hardest. If it survives, the others don't matter.

observation: Rhea subagent got stuck in an infinite text-generation loop (session 23) — kept announcing tool calls without making them. Produced no useful output for ~80 tokens of looping.
adjustment: If Rhea returns no structured output, fall back to single-pass synthesis. Don't retry the same broken pattern.

observation: Token-gate architecture (two-call handshake) came from a Rhea debate. The Doubter caught that Option 1 (advisory flag) would be ignored and Option 2 (blocking call) would timeout. The hybrid emerged from genuine adversarial pressure.
adjustment: Rhea works best on architecture decisions where there are real tradeoffs. Don't waste it on obvious calls.

observation: Rhea tends to accept proposals with modifications rather than rejecting them outright. This bias toward 'yes, but...' means bad ideas get patched instead of killed.
adjustment: The Doubter should explicitly state when the proposal should be abandoned, not just modified. 'Reject' is a valid output.
